rule: Every error is fixed AND gets an antidote: an automatic check or test that fails if the same error comes back. One line here per error, in the same PR as the fix. test_errors_register.py fails any line whose antidote does not exist.

errors.error: Three pilots (006, 007, 008) given the same Short slot by the direction's task cards
errors.fix: PR #122: one slot per pilot (night of day D at D 14:00 UTC, morning at D 20:00 UTC)

errors.error: A Short that missed its slot rolled onto another pilot's slot
errors.fix: PR #123: pending_shorts skips slots used in the ledger or reserved by another pilot

errors.error: Reused image records missing from a new pilot (task card gap): render queue would skip it
errors.fix: PR #116: hydrate_reused.py is part of every script delivery

errors.error: Offline tests existed that PR checks did not run
errors.fix: PR #123 and this PR: every test of the active folders runs on every PR

errors.error: Old plans contradicted the current rules (one told sessions to write APPROVAL.json by hand)
errors.fix: PR #121: superseded documents deleted; OPERATIONS.md lists the only directing documents

errors.error: Fallback reviewer models scored the same video very differently and could approve
errors.fix: Only the designated reviewer (gemini-3.8-flash) can PASS; others are UNKNOWN

errors.error: GitHub dropped the daily crons; tasks did not run
errors.fix: heartbeat.yml decides from the real run history and catches up

errors.error: Mining spent the Gemini quota the production review needed
errors.fix: Minings wait while production has work
history: 2026-10-19: the Gemini minings were retired (SYSTEM.md, vidIQ mining); the antidote is now that they are never dispatched

errors.error: Runner render dispatched twice for the same work
errors.fix: runner-wake: active-run guard, cooldown, per-hash attempt bound (PR #106)

errors.error: pilot-004 QA FAIL: the same background repeated after a split hold
errors.fix: Hold images assigned once over the final holds

errors.error: pilot-003: the Scripture reference stayed on screen after the closing words
errors.fix: reference_end from the KJV sentence

errors.error: Miner rows (unproven instrument) blocked a good render
errors.fix: Miner rows are informative until proven on the holdout; 2026-10-19 (#178): the miner is retired; the production audit that replaced it is report-only and can never change the status 2026-10-24: the report-only audit was removed with the Gemini reviewer; the status comes only from the Claude review and the hard rows.

errors.error: pilot-003 script (15.3 min, phrases shared with pilot-002) was written before any script acceptance existed
errors.fix: script_check.py runs on every pilot a PR touches, before images

errors.error: Nothing alerted when the queue of scripts ran short of the coming publication slots (engine could stop unnoticed)
errors.fix: Scripts kept 4 days ahead; daily report lists every slot of the next 4 days with its stage

errors.error: The final gate checked preflight against the scheduled time: an approval finishing < 15 min before the slot (or after it) would FAIL and the video would never publish, although publish.yml publishes a late approval at once
errors.fix: prepublish_gate checks preflight against preflight.effective_publish_at (the time publish.yml really uses); past Short slots are rolled forward, not a FAIL

errors.error: Scripts 003-006 broke the modeling beat order (hook 43-47 words instead of a promise spoken by 8 s; first prayer at 1:36 in 003) and acceptance did not check it
errors.fix: script_check enforces HOOK_TOO_LONG (> 20 words), FIRST_PRAYER_LATE (> 90 s), CTA_BEFORE_PAYOFF; hooks of 005/006 rewritten before render (003/004 already rendered, frozen)

errors.error: The private engine spent its 2,000 included Actions minutes with no monitoring (2026-10-19 01:21 UTC); with a US$0 spending limit every workflow stopped, including approval and publication
errors.fix: Owner pays the overage (everything stays private); 7,000 min / 30 d budget; heartbeat hourly + clock (48 beats a day instead of 72); no approval retry while the Gemini quota is spent; daily minutes report with alerts

errors.error: approve.yml runs preflight.py without a time, so a late approval was checked against the schedule's past time and failed PUBLISH_AT_NOT_AHEAD (pilot-003 at 10:01 UTC); the E16 fix covered the gate but not this step
errors.fix: preflight.main() with no time checks effective_publish_at (the time publish.yml uses: the slot, or public now when late)

errors.error: Approval was allowed to happen hours before the slot (runway alerted only at < 6 h without gate PASS); pilot-003 had 3 h between the 07:00 quota reset and its 10:00 slot and missed it on a Gemini 503
errors.fix: Owner: approve one full day ahead. Runway alerts at < 24 h without gate PASS and < 36 h without render; quality gates unchanged, no automatic provider retry

errors.error: reconcile dispatched approvals for pilot-003, 004, 005 and 006 at once; approve.yml's concurrency group keeps one pending run, so GitHub cancelled 003/004/005 and reviewed only 006 (the farthest slot), and Shorts of 005 spent the same free Gemini quota first; the quota ran out at 10:35 UTC with 003 still unapproved
errors.fix: reconcile sends only the earliest due approval; Shorts wait until no approval is pending

errors.error: Mining, Shorts selection and thumbnail analysis tried gemini-3.8-flash first (FREE_MODELS order), spending the designated reviewer's small free daily allowance; the watched reviews of pilot-003, 004 and 006 then failed with 429 QUOTA and nothing could be approved on 2026-10-19
errors.fix: structure_mining.DECISION_MODELS (the reviewer) is reserved for the watched reviews; mining, Shorts selection and thumbnail analysis use SUPPORT_MODELS (the other free models) only

errors.error: A 429 QUOTA was read as the free DAILY quota without proof: call() dropped the provider's diagnostic, review.json kept no quota id, and quota_spent() blocked retries until 07:00 UTC. Claude told the owner nothing could be approved that day; the same reviewer approved pilot-004 at 12:55 UTC. Hours lost
errors.fix: The sanitizer keeps Google's quotaId and retryDelay; call() re-raises with the diagnostic; review.json records quota_ids; only a quotaId containing PerDay waits for the reset, any other 429 is retried after 30 min

errors.error: script_check.py accepted repeated background sets: 006 at 0.529 vs 012; 008 and 010 identical to 012; 009 identical to 011. Failure surfaced only at approval after a full render and reviewer call (run 39385175032).
errors.fix: background overlap checked at script_check (first gate), same limit as approval

errors.error: Shorts tests read live pilot-006 production inputs; a re-render removed selection.json and broke main CI
errors.fix: Freeze byte-identical historical fixtures from 4ca2b3b and point the test at them without changing assertions

errors.error: Shorts passed technical QA but failed watched review for dependent openings, weak visual rhythm and unresolved endings; provider failure diagnostics were discarded.
errors.fix: PARTIAL: phase 1 validates structural openings and complete endings against full source timelines, preserves whole Scripture segments, and records strictly sanitized failure evidence. Real editing, technical QA and watched review remain pending in phase 2.

errors.error: market panel aborted on one dead playlist (404)
errors.fix: Record isolated uploads 404 per channel and preserve budget accounting; retain evidence and exit 1 when more than 25% of the panel is unavailable

errors.error: Offline counterexamples showed ignored Retry-After/RetryInfo, a sleep after the terminal HTTP503, and stale503 diagnostics after an invalid HTTP200 response. The cause of the two real provider503 responses remains UNKNOWN.
errors.fix: Opt-in designated-review HTTP policy respects complete server waits within a finite600-second budget and fixed deadline, makes at most two same-model transports, never sleeps after the final transport, and records sanitized attempt-local evidence. Existing callers and all media gates remain unchanged.

errors.error: Superseded cutover collection still had a daily trigger and produced PermissionError incidents (#249); the old archive plan also included live shared dependencies.
errors.fix: Retire the obsolete collector and other proven legacy entry points using the complete path/dependency inventory. Preserve its failure evidence without claiming an OAuth/permission repair. Keep current reporting, native QA dependencies and pending qualifications. 2026-10-23: retired workflows are deleted outright; the heartbeat may only dispatch workflows that exist.

errors.error: pilot-009 and pilot-011 failed QA image_repeat_gap after a full render: scene_target() only guaranteed 300 s between repeats for unsplit holds, but holds over HOLD_MAX are split into 18 s pieces, so 11 backgrounds came back after ~260 s.
errors.fix: still_render.holds() refuses the plan with REPEAT_GAP_VIOLATION before any encode; script_check requires BACKGROUNDS_MIN = 18, which keeps the gap with 18 s pieces.

errors.error: The voice spelled the KJV all-caps divine name GOD letter by letter ('G-O-D', pilot-008 17:36, Ezekiel 34:11).
errors.fix: pilot_render.speech_text() sends LORD/GOD/JEHOVAH/JESUS/CHRIST as capitalized words to the voice only; captions and script keep the KJV text.

errors.error: pilot-008 (12 backgrounds for 28 min) scored pacing_and_visual_variety 6.5, overall 8.0: 'a small loop of recurring AI landscape images'.
errors.fix: script_check requires at least 18 distinct backgrounds; 008, 009 and 011 get new R10 backgrounds before re-render.

errors.error: pilot-008..011 silently left the render/approval queue once their slots were more than 6 h old (reviewer 503 and QA FAILs), so reconcile stopped retrying pilot-010 and nothing reported it for a day.
errors.fix: render_queue.py stale lists passed slots with no video on YouTube (pre-standard renders excluded); the hourly clock reschedules them to the next free slot.

errors.error: Deleting the unused pilot-001 (PR #292) removed its out/qa.json; that push fired approve.yml, whose pilot lookup listed the deleted file and failed on the missing render (run 39949492128). publish.yml had the same lookup.
errors.fix: The push lookups in approve.yml and publish.yml use git diff --diff-filter=AM (added or modified only); approve ends cleanly with SKIP when a push added no render. shorts.yml stays byte-frozen by its editorial tests.

errors.error: Footage run 39948463303 took vertical 1080x1920 Commons sources as 1440p (only the height was checked) and enlarged them 2.4x to fill 2560x1440; a pillarboxed source passed the same way.
errors.fix: eligible() requires width >= 2560 as well as height >= 1440; transcode() probes the downloaded file and refuses any source smaller than the frame (SOURCE_BELOW_FRAME). The six affected clips were rejected.

antidote.contains: E51: vertical source, would be enlarged

errors.error: The first v4 render (pilot-010, run 39972041944) stopped at packaging: one credit line per footage clip (85) made a 7,577-character description, over YouTube's 5,000.
errors.fix: package_pilot.footage_credits: CC BY clips keep their own attribution line (required); clips whose licence needs no attribution are credited once per source with their authors, dropped to source and licence only when space is short.

errors.error: The same render failed QA v4 speech presence (0.844 < 0.85): the 0.45 s v4 sentence gap added ~44 s of silence that script_check's estimate (calibrated on a 0.18 s gap) did not count.
errors.fix: v4 sentence gap 0.30 s; script_check counts the extra gap per sentence for v4 pilots (the model reproduces the measured 0.844 at 0.45 s) and keeps its 0.86 margin; pilot-008 stillness pause 3.0 -> 2.0 s.

errors.error: The voice judge crashed (faster-whisper's PyAV decoder: open() got an unexpected keyword 'metadata_errors') inside 'judge | tee', and the run showed success with no verdict (run 39989082891).
errors.fix: The judge hands Whisper the 16 kHz array it already loaded (no PyAV decoding); the judge step sets pipefail; the artifact uploads even on failure.

errors.error: The voice A/B run 40000227373 hung 30 min in 'apt-get update' on the hosted Ubuntu mirror (the same mirror stall as pr-checks run 39823760082), with no step timeout.
errors.fix: voice-sample.yml installs from the official Ubuntu origins with request timeouts, command timeouts and a 25-minute step timeout, as pr-checks.yml does.

errors.error: The first v4 render (pilot-010, run 40017605277) failed the gate's driver_continuous_motion with all 178 holds in motion: the row accepted only grammars starting with 'standard-v1', and v4 writes 'standard-v4:licensed-footage...'.
errors.fix: three_stage.MOTION_GRAMMARS accepts standard-v1 and standard-v4; every hold must still move.

errors.error: HERO_RUNNER_PAT returned 401 on every heartbeat (runs 39964015145, 40005305507): the runner could not be woken, the runner-wake job failed, and no render started automatically.
errors.fix: When the runner wake-up is blocked by a rejected or missing token, the heartbeat renders on the engine itself (engine_fallback.py dispatches pilot-render-stills.yml with the engine's own token): no render waits on that credential. One active engine render at a time, at most 8 dispatches a day.

errors.error: The designated reviewer gemini-3.8-flash answered 503 for pilot-010 (runs 40017605277, 40025860740). Root cause: it does not answer our free key at all, even a 5-token text call (reviewer probe run 40036837734: timeout on 3.8-flash, 200 in < 1 s on 3.6-flash and 3.5-flash-lite; Google forum reports the same for free-tier 3.8-flash). A first fix retried within the run after 2, 5 and 10 minutes: wrong, because a down reviewer never answers and 503s may count against the daily allowance.
errors.fix: long_review asks one tiny health question first; when the reviewer does not answer, no video call is made and the review is ERROR (REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE_HEALTH_CHECK). No in-run retries. A replacement reviewer must pass reviewer_calibration (gemini-3.6-flash did not: it failed 5 of the 5 renders 3.8 passed, mean -2.2).

errors.error: Reviewer calibration run 40037346616 stopped at 'no assets match': renders that were published (004-007, 012) are no longer in the private release.
errors.fix: reviewer-calibration.yml falls back to the ledger video_id of the exact render hash and the candidate watches the public YouTube copy.

errors.error: pilot-009's render (run 40025088313) passed QA and the thumbnail ruler but could not be stored: the 16-minute 1440p file was over the 2 GiB release-asset limit (HTTP 422 'size must be less than 2147483648'), so the run failed and the render was lost.
errors.fix: migration/ci/release_video.sh stores a render larger than 1.9 GiB as parts and rejoins them, hash-verified, on download; render_pilot.sh, approve.yml, publish.yml and reviewer-calibration.yml use it. The picture is not re-encoded or reduced.

errors.error: The channel's first comment is refused while a video is still scheduled (HTTP 403), and first-comment.yml, which retries it once the video is public, was never dispatched by anything: pilots 006, 007 and 010 kept 'PENDING' first comments for up to four days.
errors.fix: render_queue reconcile prints 'comment PILOT' for the earliest public video (slot passed by 10 min, at most 7 days) with a PENDING first comment, and reconcile.yml dispatches first-comment.yml for it, one at a time (shared publish concurrency group).

errors.error: cf-images run 40047828009 failed on Cloudflare's 'used up your daily free allocation': the generator exits at the first refused image, the step fails, and any image already made in the run was never saved.
errors.fix: cf_images keeps every image made before the allocation runs out and returns DEFERRED; the workflow saves them, and a run that made none ends with a warning (the next nightly slot retries). Any other error still fails; the piped step sets pipefail (E54).

errors.error: The E57 engine fallback started a second render of pilot-009 (run 40047808539) while the runner was already rendering it on its own cron (run 40042851661): the runner never needed the rejected token, only the wake-up did.
errors.fix: engine_fallback reads the runner's public run history (no token) and renders on the engine only when the runner is neither active nor seen in the last 75 minutes; an unreadable history means no engine render.

errors.error: pilot-009's render (run 40057606889) failed the gate row hygiene_gratitude_block (2 gratitude words < 3) after a 2.5-hour render: the row depends only on the script but ran only at the gate.
errors.fix: three_stage.script_hygiene holds the script-only structure rows (amen CTA, recurring refrain, gratitude block); the gate and script_check both use it, so a script that would fail them never renders. pilot-009 gets two short thanksgiving lines.

errors.error: approve.yml recorded an approval for any review with items >= 7 and overall >= 8, while the owner floor (overall >= 9.5) was checked only at publication: a 9.0 review would be approved, publish.yml would fail on OWNER_QUALITY_POLICY_BLOCKED, and reconcile would dispatch that failing publication several times a day (found before it happened, on pilot-009's 9.0 review).
errors.fix: approve.yml runs owner_quality_policy.check (long reviewer) before writing APPROVAL.json; below the floor the status is BELOW_OWNER_FLOOR and nothing is approved or published.

errors.error: The Claude review of pilot-009 scored picture_quality 8.5 (overall 9.0, below the 9.5 floor): the v4 plan alternated footage, footage, AI still, so a third of the picture (59 of 179 scenes) was painterly AI stills cut between real footage, against the owner's real-footage standard.
errors.fix: still_render.footage_holds plans real footage only; a still is used only where the next footage shot would come back within the 5-minute repeat gap (009: 179 of 179 scenes footage). QA v4 (footage share >= 0.6) is unchanged.

errors.error: The Claude review of pilot-009 found the thumbnail's hook 'STEADY FOR TODAY' unrelated to the title's promise 'Put On God's Armor': thumbnail lines were written separately and nothing compared them with the title.
errors.fix: script_check.thumbnail_problems requires the thumbnail's hook lines to repeat a content word of the title's hook; 008, 009 and 011 get thumbnail lines from their titles.

errors.error: The first footage-only render (pilot-008, run 40077994179, after E66) failed after 2.5 h: QA marked images_open_licence_with_revision false because no generated image meant an empty model list, and the thumbnail step opened frames/001.png, which a footage-only render never writes. The QA test fixture always carried a generated image, so no test met a real footage-only manifest.
errors.fix: qa_pilot: 'every image' holds when no still is on screen (with any still the models must be recorded, as before; the frozen criteria are unchanged). package_pilot: without stills the thumbnail is drawn over the warmest first-second frame of the clips used (render_pilot.sh passes the footage folder); no source at all stops with THUMBNAIL_NO_SOURCE. Second antidote: test_thumb_check.py test_footage_only_render_takes_the_warmest_clip_frame.

errors.error: The Claude review of pilot-008 (9.0) found about a third of the picture in bright daylight (sunlit waterfalls, snowy peaks under blue sky, sunny rivers) in a 'Before You Sleep' night prayer. footage/assign.py chose night footage by theme (snow, waterfall, river, ocean, lake), and a theme says nothing about the time of day.
errors.fix: assign.py: a night pilot takes only clips whose vetting frames average luma <= 80 (the 008 daylight clips measured 82-166; 22 dark clips remain, above FOOTAGE_MIN 20); morning pilots are unchanged. 008 and 013 reassigned; 008 re-rendered.

errors.error: The Genesis 2 Short was published scheduled (private until 23:30 UTC) and its first comment came back PENDING (HTTP 403, like E61 for pilots); the E61 retry only looked at pilot-NNN ledger keys, so Bible-series episodes would have kept the comment pending forever.
errors.fix: render_queue.pending_episode_comments lists bible:<id> entries whose slot (or upload) passed 10 min to 7 days ago with a PENDING comment; reconcile.yml re-runs publish-episode.yml for them (idempotent: only the missing comment step runs; the file comes from the private release).

errors.error: pilot-008 render v2 (after E69's luma filter) still opened on a snowy valley and a sunlit waterfall and showed daylight snow, mist and a green path at 0:20-2:20 and 17:00 (Claude review 9.2, below the 9.5 floor): a clip with a dark mean luma can still show a bright daytime sky, and the night mood still drew from day themes.
errors.fix: assign.MOOD_THEMES night takes only themes that are night by nature (candle, night, rain, river) on top of the luma limit; queries.json gets night-specific searches (moon, night sky, candlelight, oil lamp, rain at night) so the night library clears FOOTAGE_MIN.

errors.error: The first real preview (pilot-011, run 40116275815) worked, and its review found three library clips with modern content that the automatic vetting had approved (a village in the valley, domestic dogs, a railed bridge on a groomed trail); its footage sheet put all 63 clips in one 960x15120 image, unreadable when opened.
errors.fix: The three clips are REJECTED in the library (reasons recorded) and pilot-011's footage was reassigned, so the new script is previewed again; render_pilot.sh writes the footage sheet in pages of 12 clips (footage-sheet-NN.jpg).

errors.error: After the preview gate (#340) heartbeat run 40120253555 failed: render_queue.py imports preview_gate, but heartbeat.yml and the public runner run it as 'python3 -I -B', which leaves the script's own directory off sys.path (ModuleNotFoundError). The unit tests imported the module without -I and passed, so every scheduled preview and render dispatch would have stopped.
errors.fix: render_queue.py puts its own directory on sys.path before importing preview_gate; a test runs render_queue.py in every mode exactly as the scheduler does (python3 -I -B).

errors.error: pilot-011's preview never converged: each reassignment after rejecting modern clips (3, then 4, then 7) brought clips nobody had seen into the next preview, some of them modern again (ski huts, a village with a church, wind turbines).
errors.fix: Every clip kept on a preview review is marked claude_seen in the library; assign.choose uses only seen clips once the mood has FOOTAGE_MIN of them, so the next preview of a reassigned script shows no unseen clip.

errors.error: The Claude review of pilot-011 found its description crediting 'original HeroVerse images made with open-licence AI image models' and the package marking ai_generated_visuals, while the footage-only render (E68) uses no AI still: package_pilot.py added the illustration credit to every v2 package.
errors.fix: package_pilot credits and discloses AI stills only when the manifest has images; a footage-only package credits the footage and says the narration voice is AI. pilot-011's package text was regenerated with the fix (title, tags and thumbnail unchanged).

errors.error: The pilot-013 night-prayer preview opened (0:12-0:20) on an autumn forest creek filmed by day: its mean luma (33) passed the E69 limit and its theme 'river' was still a night theme after E71.
errors.fix: assign.py: night takes only candle, night and rain (river is shot by day like waterfall). A window-pane rain clip with a daytime sky was rejected in the library. pilot-013's footage was reassigned from Claude-seen night clips.

errors.error: pilot-008's render (run 40151353875) failed the full-file scan (black_picture 0.57 s > 0.5 s at 6:03; also 1:26, 8:22, 12:57, 15:16): the 'starry sky, mountains, mist' night clip goes 98 % black for up to 1.2 s once the render's footage grade is applied. Library vetting measured only the mean luma of 5 frames (32, 24, 34, 26, 22), so the clip was approved, kept on two previews and assigned to pilot-008 and pilot-013.
errors.fix: footage.vet measures the longest near-black run after cinematic.GRADE with the scan's own blackdetect criteria (pic_th 0.98) and rejects a clip at >= 0.5 s (BLACK_RUN_AFTER_GRADE). The 26 usable night clips were measured: only this one fails; it is REJECTED and pilot-008 and pilot-013 are reassigned (new previews follow).

errors.error: pilot-009's preview (run 40170360356) showed 7 clips the footage library had already REJECTED (Fife Creek boardwalk with railings, Sonoma Creek concrete weir, village houses in the valley, and 4 more); pilot-014's earlier preview did too. script_check flagged them (FOOTAGE_NOT_VETTED), but render_queue picked pilots for preview and render without reading the library, so a stale assignment reached a preview and could reach a 2.5 h render.
errors.fix: render_queue.unvetted_footage lists a script's clips the library does not approve; preview and render skip such a pilot (one shared next_render rule, now also used by the runner wake and the engine fallback, which had their own copies) and the new 'reassign' mode lists it for the clock (CLAUDE_REVIEW.md), which reassigns with footage/assign.py. pilot-009 is reassigned from seen morning clips (script_check PASS).

errors.error: The owner saw that the long's footage was landscapes unrelated to the narration. still_render.footage_holds cycled script['footage'] in list order across the whole video, and footage/assign.py chose clips by mood (night or morning themes) only, so a story long would show a waterfall over the serpent's words; nothing in the gate tied a clip to what is being said (the Shorts already search a clip per line).
errors.fix: Story segments name the clips mined for their words (segments[].shots, queried per segment from pilot-NNN/beats-N.json through footage.yml's new queries input); footage_holds fills each segment's cuts with its own clips first and never puts one segment's clip over another's words; script_check.picture_problems refuses a spoken segment with fewer matched shots than its cuts (PICTURE_UNMATCHED), a shot missing from footage and any clip no segment named (FOOTAGE_NOT_MATCHED_TO_WORDS); the preview review checks each clip against its segment's words.

errors.error: The first TikTok mirror post through Buffer (run 40213060551, Genesis 2) was refused by Buffer's GraphQL validation: the createPost input was written from third-party notes (assets as {videos: [{url}]}) without reading the schema. Nothing was created; the ledger recorded FAILED (1 of 3).
errors.fix: discover mode now prints the input types createPost accepts (introspection of CreatePostInput and the input types it references), and the post input is set from that evidence before the next post; the refusal message is kept long enough to read.

errors.error: Both pilot-015 footage runs (40209722971, 40209725019) died on their first clip: footage.py's vetting calls graded_black_run (E77), which imports cinematic and numpy, but footage.yml installs only ffmpeg, tesseract and PIL. E77's tests ran where numpy exists, so the workflow gap was not seen.
errors.fix: footage.yml installs python3-numpy; a test reads the workflow and checks it installs every package the vetting imports. The two beat runs are dispatched again.

errors.error: The unofficial Pavo stream returned error 009999 when the request omitted the platform and client-time metadata used by the official web client. The request created no generation turn and did not change the credit balance.
errors.fix: The Pavo video adapter sends the official platform, timezone, client time and language headers, keeps its own HeroVerse User-Agent, and only submits after an exact zero-credit quote. One live 5-second Flash generation then succeeded.

errors.error: Pre-merge tests found that float conversion could round an extremely small positive Pavo price to zero and allow generation. No affected code was deployed.
errors.fix: Parse JSON decimals without float loss and compare exact Decimal values; reject negative, nonfinite, malformed and unrepresentable prices before creating a conversation.

errors.error: Pre-merge tests found that a late GenerationStart could be accepted and a trickling SSE line or HTTP chunk header could outlive the stream budget. read1 alone did not interrupt HTTPResponse's internal readline. No affected code was deployed.
errors.fix: Read bounded chunks, check the deadline before interpreting events, and cancel the stream-body socket after 30 seconds. A local socket-pair regression reproduces incomplete chunk metadata. Return unknown with the original conversation ID instead of resubmitting.

errors.error: Footage run 40218507819 (pilot-015 beats-1) failed at its upload: v0.0.0-cloud-assets-20261013 reached GitHub's limit of 1000 assets per release (HTTP 422 file_count). Every workflow wrote to that one release, so every new asset (footage, stills, renders, Shorts, episodes) would fail from then on.
errors.fix: migration/ci/assets.sh keeps the engine's assets in several releases, newest first: uploads go to the newest (v0.0.0-cloud-assets-20261025, created on first use), downloads try newest first and fall back, names/which/delete cover every release, and a warning fires past 950 assets so a new tag is added before the next one fills. Every workflow and CI script goes through it; records (cf-images, footage) carry release_tag and tiktok.yml/agnes-clip.yml/characters.py build public URLs from the release that holds the file. No asset was deleted or moved.

errors.error: The TikTok mirror's 23:41 UTC cron run on 2026-10-25 never started (GitHub dropped the scheduled run), so no Short went to TikTok for 8 hours after their YouTube slots; the mirror only ran twice a day, so one dropped run meant half a day late.
errors.fix: tiktok.yml runs every 20 minutes (7,27,47 * * * *): a Short goes to TikTok within ~20 minutes of its YouTube slot and a dropped run is covered by the next; one Short per run keeps posts apart while a backlog clears. The hourly clock also dispatches tiktok.yml when a published Short is still not mirrored.

errors.error: episode_build.compose_shots refused the Genesis 7 example plan with KEEPER_NOT_ON_HIS_LINE k-close: two Keeper shots in a row (insight, then close) left the 0.35 s silence between their lines owned by no shot, so the second Keeper picture could not start on its first word. Found by the offline compose test before any run; no affected code was deployed.
errors.fix: The silence after a line belongs to the next run of scenes or, when the next shot is the Keeper again, to the Keeper shot before it (he holds the gap; KEEPER_MARGIN 0.6 s covers it, and the closing Keeper's audio limit is 10.2 s so line + tail + margin fit a 12 s clip). Every Keeper picture still starts exactly on his first word, from the start of his clip at normal speed.

errors.error: Structure mining counted videos below the winner bar as winners: Steelshort (breakout 6.2) in the bible-story-short candidate, and 3acset3y_Aw (46.41) and DKBkPbJ73xU (13.34) in the validated spoken-prayer-short. errors.error: The owner saw 'Erro ao carregar legendas' in the YouTube app on 8heTdP0LllM (pilot-008, now private). publish_video.py sent the SRT with captions.insert, took HTTP 200 as done and recorded captions: true; nothing ever read whether YouTube served the track (captions.list snippet.status serving/syncing/failed), so a failed or stuck track could pass silently on every long. The resume check also took any English track, the automatic ASR one included, as 'already inserted', which would skip our upload. Offline evidence: the SRT rebuilt for each of the 11 captioned prayer longs (002, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 010, 011, 012, 013, 014; each manifest's hash is its ledger key) is valid (numbering, timing format, blank-line separators, monotonic and non-overlapping, inside the video, no empty cue, ASCII/UTF-8 without BOM, LF) and its multipart media part is byte-exact; the SRT is therefore not shown to be the cause. The live cause (failed track, still syncing, private-video playback in the app, or the ASR track) is decided by the captions-audit run, not claimed here.
errors.fix: publish/captions.py builds (byte-identical for valid input), validates strictly and frames the SRT; publish_video.py validates before captions.insert (CAPTIONS_SRT_INVALID), records the track id, polls captions.list a bounded number of times (captions.WAIT_CALLS, 50 units each, inside preflight's LONG_UNITS) and records captions_status; failed or not listed fails the run with CAPTIONS_FAILED after the ledger and receipt are written; still syncing is recorded with a warning and read again by a re-run, which also verifies the legacy entries; only our standard English track counts, never ASR. preflight.py validates the exact SRT against output_seconds. channel-privacy.yml gains captions-audit (read-only receipt channel/captions-audit-<run>.json) and captions-repair (only a reviewed captions-repair-plan.json; delete our failed track, insert, wait), both by hand only. Review of #424, each with a test that failed first: a recorded failed track is re-inserted at most once a run (delete ours, never ASR; then verify), so a failure no longer fails every re-run; a resumed upload whose legacy manifest fails the strict SRT check records CAPTIONS_SRT_INVALID as a warning, uploads nothing and lets the chain go on (a new upload is still refused before upload); captions-repair writes the new track id and status into the publish ledger entry (committed with the receipt) and writes the receipt after every delete and insert; a plan longer than MAX_PLAN (from the wait and the job timeout) is refused; PAST_VIDEO_END compares against the duration rounded to the millisecond; the english scope uses channel_privacy.language and the uploads paging is one helper, channel_privacy.channel_uploads.

errors.fix: The build's rules are pure functions the early stages call: episode_build.retime_plan / plan_layout / compose_prediction / predict (lines_step uses them), reference_keys / reference_problems (request() uses the same order) and request_problems; plan_check runs predict and reference_problems on its estimate ("BUILD ...") and refuses under --strict the path episode.yml refuses (path_problems, PLAN_PATH the workflow's own pattern). generate_step validates every request offline before the first generation (REQUESTS_REFUSED). `episode_build.py preflight` runs locally with 0 Actions and 0 credits: plan_check --strict, characters and their next step, cf-images used today against ~44, the pinned Kokoro voice and episode_build lines, the compose on the measured layout, refs and requests, and each talking LINE against evidence/pavo/setups.json (the lips rate belongs to the line, #419: fewer than 6 direct generations of that line is PROBE_REQUIRED, a chance under 0.9 within 6 attempts is PROBE_RATE_LOW; genesis-07's Keeper lines read 0 of 15, 0 of 15 and 1 of 3 and are BLOCKED); episode.yml's first step runs verify-preflight (a PASS report committed for that exact plan and characters.json), and hookify blocks an episode dispatch not chained to verify-preflight and a cf-images pilot input of the wrong form. `check-record` runs publish_episode's rules on the record before publish-episode.yml. errors.error: genesis-07 (run 40341856955, Keeper voice-over) composed cleanly but its review put it under the 9.5 floor: scene shots anachronistic for the days of Noah. s-walker (126-134 s) a man in a modern long coat with a glass kerosene lantern on a cobbled street of European stone buildings, men in top hats around him; s-family (147-153 s) a European town with church towers on the horizon, European dress. The per-shot frame sheet of the composed file (evidence/pavo/20261026/period/review.json) found six more: s-wind a town with spires across green fields ("the road out of the city"), s-theft a stone village with chimneys and cypresses, s-quarrel a peaked cap, s-ruins glass mason jars, s-children canvas bell tents and brimmed hats, s-knife plastered walls and an iron wall sconce. 8 of 30 scene shots. Root cause: the scene prompts carried no period setting (only 'tents', 'lane', 'city'), so Pavo filled each lane and horizon with what it knows best, and no gate checked the period: plan_check had no rule, and the review was the first place the picture's age was seen.
errors.fix: plan_check: every scene prompt (God's voice-over and a speaking character's shot too; not the Keeper's own campfire) states its story's period word for word, one shared constant: PERIOD_SETTING ('The ancient Near East before the flood: only goat-hair tents, open fires and torches on the open plain.') and PERIOD_EXCLUDE ('No stone buildings, towers, churches, glass lanterns, modern clothing or roads.'), else SCENE_PERIOD_MISSING; with both sentences taken out it names nothing the period excludes (PERIOD_AVOID, review of #426 with the root-cause words: city, lane, room, table, street, road, building, brick, wall but a tent's, house, dome, tower, church, town, village, lantern, glass lantern or jar, coat, hat, peaked cap), else SCENE_PERIOD_CONFLICT. The period is the plan's `period` (a preset: eden, before-the-flood, the-flood; or its own setting, exclusions and avoid list, validated, the shared list when it gives none; a malformed or unknown one is PERIOD_INVALID, never passed over) or its passage's, every chapter of it (STORY_PERIODS Genesis 1-3, 4-6, 7-9; a passage across two periods is PERIOD_AMBIGUOUS until the plan sets one); none is SCENE_PERIOD_MISSING, one message (missing_period). One helper, plan_period_problems, runs in plan_check and long_plan_check (the arc-01 long draft carries the eden period, three prompts reworded); episode_build.request refuses the same by period_refusal. Registered class A; the review mapping has period_accuracy under figure_and_background_integrity. genesis-07's plan: period before-the-flood; the eight anachronistic shots rewritten (s-walker a robed man with a small clay oil lamp among the tents; s-family a hillside path above the camp of tents, no town), 15 more reworded for the root-cause words (city of tents -> camp of tents, lane -> path between the tents, a quiet room -> inside a goat-hair tent), every scene prompt carries the period: the resume regenerates the 30 scene and God clips and keeps the 3 voice-over Keeper clips. Probed first with direct 0-credit Pavo clips (evidence/pavo/20261026/period/probes.json): 'mud-brick' put towers or a domed tower behind 4 of 8; 'clay lamps' drew a metal-and-glass candle lantern into 3 of 11 night shots; the plan's wording 4 of 4 period-true. And episode.yml `regenerate` (shot ids, with resume_run, checked by episode_build check-regenerate before any secret, passed through the env, recorded in report.json) redoes only the clips the frame review rejects, with no prompt edited to force it.

errors.error: genesis-07 Short build run 40357197063 (episode.yml) passed every gate, but Claude's visual review rejected s-well: the Pavo clip was a wide picture letterboxed inside the 9:16 frame, black bars above and below (ffmpeg cropdetect on the composed 1080x1920 file at t=22.5 s: crop=1080:1062:0:428, about 22 % black at each edge). Root cause: clip_check, the per-clip check every Pavo shot passes before the compose, measured only black at the clip's start and end, resolution and frame rate; nothing looked for black bands inside the frame, so a letterboxed generation was kept as clean.
errors.fix: clip_check.check measures bars: BAR_FRAMES (5) frames sampled across the clip, scaled to a 90-pixel short side, each row and column's peak luma; a bar is a run of rows (columns) from an edge whose every pixel is at or under BAR_LUMA (24). A clip whose smallest bar over the sampled frames is over BAR_SHARE (4 %) at BOTH opposite edges (top and bottom, or left and right) is flagged LETTERBOX_BARS, so episode_build's attempt loop (make_shot) generates the shot anew like BLACK_START; an all-black frame is left to BLACK_START/BLACK_END. Both edges and every frame keep dark night shots clean: measured over all 32 Pavo clips in migration/evidence/pavo (the darkest, the Keeper probes at mean luma 48, and genesis-06's oil-lamp night shot), the lamp shot darkened to near black (eq brightness -0.35), and a black sky over a lit camp: no flag; the lamp shot padded to s-well's shape (22 % each side) and a pillarboxed one: flagged. Registered class C (refusal_registry.json) and in the review mapping of picture_quality. genesis-07's s-well is redone by the resume with regenerate=s-well.
